The next morning you see one missed call, no name, no context, and nobody calls back. Now the same night with recovery running. The missed call is detected, and a text goes out four seconds later. At nine fifteen the customer replies: no heat at all, house is fifty-four, can someone come tomorrow. It isn't life-safety, so it gets booked instead of escalated. They take the seven thirty window. And at seven-oh-two the next morning, the job is on your board with the address, the symptom, and the whole thread.

scenes.vo: This is what actually goes out, word for word. Sorry we missed your call, this is the after-hours line. Is this an emergency, or can we get you on the schedule for tomorrow? They answer. We offer the first two openings, and tell them to text back URGENT if the house drops below fifty tonight. They pick seven thirty. It's booked, and they'll get a text when the tech is on the way. None of this sounds like a machine, because we write the wording with you before it ever goes live.
